title: To my dear daughter Naseem, going abroad
titleOriginal: اپنی عزیزہ بیٹی نسیم اختر دے نال
takeaway: Travel well, and remember that you carry your country's name with you.
scene: The poet's daughter Naseem Akhtar is leaving to live in another country. He gives her his blessing and some advice.

original: غیر ملک نوں جاندیا جا خیریں سفر سنت حبیب یزدان دی اے
اللہ پاک دی قدرت دا پتہ لگدا حکم اوس دا وچ قرآن وی اے
transliteration: Ghair mulk nu jaandiya ja khairen, safar sunnat Habib-e-Yazdaan di ae
Allah Paak di qudrat da pata lagda, hukam os da vich Quran vi ae
translation: You who are going abroad, go safely: travel is a sunnah of God's Beloved.
Travelling, you discover the power of God; His command to do so is in the Qur'an too.
couplets.story: He tells his daughter to go safely. Travelling is something the Prophet himself did. When you travel, you see how amazing God's world is, and the Qur'an itself tells people to travel and look around.

original: سفر نال عزت دولت شان لبھدی ایہدے نال توقیر انسان دی اے
قول فعل آپ دا پتہ دیوے احمدؔ شہرن ایہہ پاکستان دی اے
transliteration: Safar naal izzat daulat shaan labhdi, ehde naal tauqeer insaan di ae
Qaul fail aap da pata deve, Ahmad, shehran eh Pakistan di ae
translation: Through travel you can find honour, wealth and standing; it raises a person's dignity.
Ahmad says: let your words and deeds show who you are, for this is a daughter (citizen) of Pakistan.
couplets.story: Travel can bring respect, success and a better life. But he reminds her: the way you speak and act will show people where you're from. You are a daughter of Pakistan, so make it proud.

deeper: The Qur'an repeatedly invites people to 'travel through the land and see' (e.g. 29:20), and the poet uses this to bless his daughter's journey. Calling travel 'a sunnah of the Beloved' links it to the Prophet's own migration.
why: Many families today have a child who moves abroad. This is what a proud, loving father wants to say when they go.
prompt: If you moved to another country, how would you want people there to see where you come from?
notes: 'Shehran' is read as 'female citizen'; the line may also mean 'this is Pakistan's honour'.
